subject: CrossCloud ISV sync: integration tradeoffs & prelist exception request
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: partners@crosscloud.io
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: CrossCloud ISV sync: integration tradeoffs & prelist exception request

Hi Liam / CrossCloud partnerships team,

Thanks again for taking time last week. We ran the internal scoping for the CrossCloud connector and have two asks before we can schedule a formal prelist review:

- Can CrossCloud accept a light-weight tokenized entitlement model (no full marketplace entitlement flow) for an initial pilot? This avoids a catalog-level entitlement change but preserves billing hooks.
- We need a short exception to the standard prelist network cert requirement for our staging environment (we can share a signed attestation and a firewall rule set).

High-level constraints: our Dedicated customers expect predictable latency; Marissa will validate whether the KV-cache approach we discussed preserves SLOs in early tests. Ben — can you confirm if the pilot pricing/commit we discussed is OK to present?

I've attached a one-page checklist and the integration spec draft. Proposal: quick sync Thursday to close blockers and list action owners.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships (Marketplace)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: integration_spec_v1.xlsx, prelist_checklist.pdf

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crosscloud.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@crosscloud.io
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: CrossCloud ISV sync: integration tradeoffs & prelist exception request

Vanessa — thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick notes:

- Pilot entitlement: that seems reasonable from our side provided we have a technical rollout that prevents cross-tenant leakage. Our security lead (cc'd on future emails) will need the KV-cache and token flow diagrams.
- Prelist exception: we can open a temporary exemption but will require a signed SOC2 attestation and the staging firewall rules; we can accept a 30-day window for the pilot.

We can do the Thursday sync at 15:00 UTC if that works. I'll bring our ISV integrations engineer.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Partner Programs, CrossCloud
liam.oconnor@crosscloud.io

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 13:27:00 +0100
Subject: Re: CrossCloud ISV sync: integration tradeoffs & prelist exception request

Noted — pilot pricing is OK from my side as discussed: 3 month pilot, nominal reserved capacity, usage-based overage. We should capture the seats/throughput we expect in the mutual action plan.

Marissa: can you confirm whether the KV-cache approach adds any additional audit/telemetry hooks we need to surface for CrossCloud's security team? If not, we should be explicit that the pilot includes "prefix caching only" and that persistent KV replication is off.

Karthik: please be prepared to call out any API surface changes (auth headers, new entitlement token) on Thursday. If we can't meet that timeline, we should postpone the prelist exception request.

Ben
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crosscloud.io>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 09:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: CrossCloud ISV sync: integration tradeoffs & prelist exception request

Liam / team — attaching the lightweight diagram and the short telemetry checklist (see attachment names). Quick points:

- Approach: prefix KV caching only (no cross-tenant KV sync). That keeps the KV-layer ephemeral and within customer boundaries.
- Audit hooks: we will emit token-binding events and per-request latency samples to our Console telemetry. We can provide a short export (CSV) for the pilot security review.

Attachments referenced: integration_spec_v1.xlsx (sheet: caching-model), prelist_checklist.pdf

> - Prelist exception: we can open a temporary exemption but will require a signed SOC2 attestation and the staging firewall rules; we can accept a 30-day window for the pilot.
>

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@crosscloud.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 16:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: CrossCloud ISV sync: integration tradeoffs & prelist exception request

Thanks everyone — quick recap and owners from today's sync: 

- Action: CrossCloud to accept pilot token flow with prefix caching only. Owner: Liam O'Connor (CrossCloud). Due: 2028-07-05.
- Action: Redwood to produce signed SOC2 attestation and firewall rule snapshot for staging. Owner: Vanessa Ortiz / Security. Due: 2028-06-30.
- Action: Marissa to share CSV telemetry export template and minimal API change notes. Owner: Marissa Cole. Due: 2028-06-29.
- Action: Ben to draft the mutual action plan including pilot pricing/commit. Owner: Ben Carter. Due: 2028-06-28.

We agreed CrossCloud will treat the pilot as a temporary prelist exemption (30 days) and will re-evaluate on success metrics (latency, error rate, billing hooks). If any security redlines emerge, CrossCloud reserves the right to pause.

Attaching the updated integration spec (v1.1) and the prelist checklist we've filled partially. Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/IMS-452

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships (Marketplace)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: integration_spec_v1.xlsx (updated), prelist_checklist.pdf
